primary_source_citation.title: FEMA National Preparedness Goal Technical Reference: The Five Phases of Emergency Management (FEMA Framework)

1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Every $1 invested in pre-disaster hazard mitigation saves an average of $6 in future disaster response and rebuilding costs.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. Prevention & Mitigation (Before): Eliminate or reduce hazard impact ahead of time: smoke/CO alarms, strapping water heaters, clearing storm drains.
2. Preparedness & Family Drills (Before): Build 72-hour Go-Bags, designate an out-of-state phone relay contact, and practice two exit routes per room.
3. Immediate Response (During Crisis): Protect life safety first, account for all family and patrol members via buddy system, and avoid downed lines.
4. Short & Long-Term Recovery (After): Restore utilities safely, document damage with photos, check on elderly neighbors, and debrief lessons learned.
1.worked_field_example: Step 1: Read the official Emergency Preparedness Requirement 1 prompt carefully and underline every action verb. Step 2: Apply the field rule of thumb (Every $1 invested in pre-disaster hazard mitigation saves an average of $6 in future disaster response and rebuilding costs.). Step 3: Verify each measurement or checkpoint against FEMA National Preparedness Goal reference criteria and record your findings in your Scout Workbook.
1.counselor_tabletop_demo: 3-Minute Troop Tabletop Demo (Req 1): Display emergency_prep_five_phases_cycle_v46_diagram.png on screen, divide Scouts into buddy pairs for a 90-second hands-on walkthrough of 'The Five Phases of Emergency Management (FEMA Framework)', and have each pair state the key threshold (Every $1 invested in pre-disaster hazard mitigation saves an average of $6 in future disaster response and rebuilding costs.) in their own words before sign-off.

2.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Unity of Command + Span of Control (3 to 7 people per supervisor, optimal 5) prevents chaos during every emergency.
core_mechanism_bullets: Incident Commander (Single Point of Command): Sets overall incident objectives, safety priorities, and coordinates directly with fire, police, and EMS.
Safety Officer (Authority to Stop Unsafe Acts): Continuously monitors scene hazards, heat/cold stress, hydration, and strict Scouting Youth Protection.
Operations & Logistics Sections: Operations runs safe Scout support tasks (shelter canteen, runner messages); Logistics manages gear, food, radios.
Planning & Check-In Accountability: Maintains written roster check-in/check-out logs so every Scout and volunteer is accounted for every hour.

primary_source_citation.title: FEMA Ready.gov & American Red Cross Technical Reference: Safe Rescue Hierarchy & Utility Emergency Shutoff Rules

3.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Never become a second victim: use Reach-Throw-Row before entering water, and never flip light switches if you smell gas.
core_mechanism_bullets: Reach - Throw - Row - Go Ladder: Always extend a pole/branch or throw a buoyant line from shore first before committing a trained rescuer.
Downed Power Lines (35+ Foot Rule): Treat every fallen wire as energized; keep back at least 35 feet and shuffle feet together without lifting.
Natural Gas & Carbon Monoxide: Rotten-egg mercaptan odor or CO alarm: evacuate outdoors immediately without touching switches; call 911 outside.
72-Hour Go-Kit Core Standard: 1 gallon of water per person per day (3 gal total), non-perishable food, headlamp, NOAA radio, first aid, meds.

primary_source_citation.title: NASAR & National Park Service SAR Technical Reference: Backcountry Lost-Person Search & Rescue (SAR) Containment

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Three sharp whistle blasts is the universal international distress call; mark Point Last Seen (PLS) immediately.
core_mechanism_bullets: Phase 1: Freeze Point Last Seen (PLS): Flag the exact spot and time the missing person was last seen so boot tracks and scent clues stay undisturbed.
Phase 2: Containment & Hasty Teams: Post lookouts at trail junctions, road crossings, and creek bridges while fast teams check high-probability trails.
Phase 3: High-Probability Clue Search: Searchers look for physical clues (footprints, wrapper, broken twigs) because clues outnumber people 100 to 1.
Phase 4: Safe Scout Mobilization Boundaries: Scouts serve in supervised base-camp logistics, communications, and perimeter support within council safety rules.
